corrected_claim: Hepatitis B virus has an unusual circular DNA genome that is not fully double-stranded, and it is one of a few known pararetroviruses.

note: Page says 'unusual', not 'unique among human viruses'

claim: Termite mounds in Australia can be over 4 meters tall and are oriented along a north-south axis to regulate internal temperature—earning them the name 'magnetic termites.'
corrected_claim: Australia's magnetic (or compass) termites build wedge-shaped mounds up to 4 m tall, aligned north-south so they expose less surface to the midday sun when the nest might overheat.
quote: The mounds built by this termite can be up to 4 m (13 ft) tall ... the common names derive from the fact that the wedge-shaped mound is aligned with its main axis running north and south. ... exposing less surface to the sun at midday when the nest might overheat.
note: page says up to 4 m, not over 4 m

claim: Onions make you cry because cutting them releases syn-propanethial-S-oxide, a sulfur compound that irritates the eyes.
note: Food science page is a general overview and does not mention this

claim: The word 'avocado' comes from Nahuatl 'ahuacatl' meaning 'testicle' — referring to the fruit's shape.
note: Source says the 'testicle' original meaning is a popular myth; original meaning reconstructed as 'avocado', used as euphemism for testicle

claim: Quantal response equilibrium relaxes Nash equilibrium by allowing probabilistic choice — better responses are more likely but not certain, fitting experimental data better.
corrected_claim: Quantal response equilibrium is a game-theory solution concept with bounded rationality: the probability of choosing a strategy rises with its payoff, so every strategy is played with some probability, unlike in a strict Nash equilibrium.
quote: it provides an equilibrium notion with bounded rationality. ... The probability of any particular strategy being chosen is positively related to the payoff from that strategy.
note: Page does not say it fits experimental data better; it says QRE is not a refinement of Nash

claim: Invasive chestnut blight and Dutch elm disease are plant pathogens that have devastated North American forests.
corrected_claim: Chestnut blight and Dutch elm disease are plant pathogens with serious impacts on forest ecosystems.
quote: Chestnut blight (Cryphonectria parasitica) and Dutch elm disease ... are plant pathogens with serious impacts.
note: 'Devastated North American forests' not stated directly

claim: In 2006, the first imperfect invisibility cloak was demonstrated using gradient-index metamaterials at microwave frequencies.
corrected_claim: At microwave frequencies, the first, imperfect invisibility cloak was realized in 2006.
quote: At microwave frequencies, the first, imperfect invisibility cloak was realized in 2006.
note: Page does not tie the 2006 cloak to gradient-index metamaterials

claim: AT&T was forbidden from entering the computer business by a 1956 antitrust case — so they gave Unix source code to anyone who asked, spurring its adoption.
quote: As a 1956 antitrust case forbade AT&T from entering the computer business ... AT&T provided the operating system's source code to anyone who asked.

claim: Histoplasma capsulatum hides inside macrophages — the immune cells meant to kill it become its home.
corrected_claim: In infected tissue, Histoplasma capsulatum yeast cells are characteristically seen clustered inside phagocytic cells such as macrophages.
quote: are characteristically seen forming in clusters within phagocytic cells, including ... histiocytes and other macrophages, as well as monocytes.
note: Page shows yeasts inside macrophages but does not discuss evading killing

claim: Termite guts contain protozoa that digest cellulose—without these gut symbionts, termites would starve even with a stomach full of wood.
corrected_claim: Termites rely primarily on a symbiotic gut community of bacteria and flagellate protists that provides the enzymes to digest cellulose.
quote: Termites rely primarily upon a symbiotic microbial community that includes bacteria and flagellate protists ... This community provides the enzymes that digests the cellulose, allowing the insects to absorb the end products
note: Page does not say termites would starve without symbionts; higher termites have no protozoa.

claim: Garlic's characteristic smell comes from allicin, which only forms when garlic cells are damaged—crushing releases more flavor than slicing.
note: Food science page is a general overview and does not mention this

claim: The word 'ketchup' likely comes from Chinese 'kê-tsiap' meaning 'fermented fish sauce' — the original was nothing like modern ketchup.
corrected_claim: One theory traces 'ketchup' to a Hokkien word from southern China meaning the brine of pickled fish or shellfish, though the word's etymology is unclear with multiple competing theories.
quote: The etymology of the word ketchup is unclear; there are multiple competing theories. ... Another theory is that the word derives from one of two words from Hokkien of the Fujian region of coastal southern China.
note: Page says etymology unclear; Hokkien meaning is pickled-fish brine

claim: Spoiler effects occur when a losing candidate's presence changes who wins — Ralph Nader in Florida 2000 potentially cost Gore the election, a flaw of plurality voting.
quote: The 2000 U.S. Presidential Election in Florida ... it is plausible (see Magee 2003) that Al Gore (A) would have won without Ralph Nader (B) in the election ... Vote splitting is the most common cause of spoiler effects in FPP.
note: Page lists 2000 among elections most consistently cited as spoiled by third-party candidates.
